new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (PDF 1.4, 4 pp., Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-08-26, text layer present; in the same directory records it as the Wayback 2024-05-18 capture of sil.org reapdata = SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42309). extracted text per page confirms the locator: physical page 2 (running header 'Melamela OPD Printed: August 27, 2004 Page 2') ends with the section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' whose full text is exactly: 'Stress is predictable in that it generally falls on the penultimate syllable. Stressed vowels are normally lengthened. Vowel lengthening is not phonemic.' -- verbatim as quoted (only line wrapping differs). I independently decoded the legacy SIL-IPA9…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable of the word (hedged 'generally'); the stressed vowel is phonetically lengthened, and vowel length is not phonemic. The OPD's own phonetic transcriptions place the stress mark before the penult, e.g. luumu [luʔ'uːmu̥] 'niggardly', ilisi [i'liːsi̥] 'to rise', aani [ʔaʔ'aːni] 'to eat'.
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the only hedge is 'generally'. No discussion of how vowel sequences/diphthongs (ei, ai, ou, ui listed as CVV syllables) count for the penult.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a 4-page OPD; examples are isolated citation forms. No phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Source titles the language 'Melamela (Meramera) Language [MXM]', West New Britain Province; Melamela is the older/Catholic-mission spelling of Meramera (glottocode mera1242, ISO mxm). No dialect is specified; data collected by H. Ohtsuba (SIL) from 1986 onward on the north coast of New Britain straddling the WNB/ENB border.
